## Paths

I'm going to set this up to dump data to the QAEL WERP share for now. Unfortunately, that calls itself something different for each of us.

```{r}
#| include: false

if (Sys.info()['user'] == 'galen') {
  qaelpath <- '~/../Deakin University/QAEL - WERP in house - WERP'
} else if (Sys.info()['user'] == 'Georgiad') {
  qaelpath <- '~/Deakin University/QAEL - WERP - WERP'
} else if (Sys.info()['user'] == 'georgiad') {
  qaelpath <- 'C:/Users/georgiad/Deakin University/QAEL - WERP - WERP'
} else if (Sys.info()['user'] == 'Admin') {
  qaelpath <- 'C:/Users/Admin/Deakin University/QAEL - WERP in house - WERP'
} else {
  rlang::abort("YOU'RE NOT GALEN. PUT IN YOUR PATH TO QAEL-WERP")
}

# python can't use the tildes, so have to expand
qaelpath <- path.expand(qaelpath)

# Outer directory for project data
project_dir = file.path(qaelpath, 'Toolkit', 'macq-data')

# Hydrographs (expected to exist already; created here with Ash_data_sorting.qmd)
hydro_dir = file.path(qaelpath, 'Toolkit/AshData/historical')

# Generated data
data_type_dir <- file.path(project_dir, 'historic')
Models <- c('Mk5', 'Mk4', 'Mk4a') #'Mk5a', 

# module_output
ewr_results <- c('module_output', 'EWR') 

# outputs of aggregator. There may be multiple modules
agg_results <- c('aggregator_output')
aggregations <-  c('sdl_EWRs', 'sdl_objective', 'sdl_objective_simple','sdl_target' , 'sdl_theme')

sdl_economic_dir <- file.path(data_type_dir, "sdl_economics")

comp_results <- file.path(data_type_dir, 'comparer_output') 
```

## Scenario info

```{r}
#| label: scenario-info
#| include: false

dig1 <- function(x) {
  paste0(sprintf("%.1f", x))
}
dig2 <- function(x) {
  paste0(sprintf("%.2f", x))
  }

print(file.path(hydro_dir,'scenario_metadata.yml'))

scenarios <- yaml::read_yaml(file.path(hydro_dir,                                     
                                       'scenario_metadata.yml'))

scenarios <- scenarios |>  
  tibble::as_tibble() 

# set a sceneorder
scenarios <- scenarios |>
    dplyr::mutate(Rainfall = as.numeric(Rainfall),
                Evapotranspiration = as.numeric(Evapotranspiration),
                licvolfactor = as.numeric(licvolfactor))|>
  dplyr::arrange(desc(Rainfall), Evapotranspiration, desc(licvolfactor))


sceneorder <- scenarios$scenario

scenarios <- scenarios |>
  mutate(names_scenario = paste("SR",dig1(Rainfall), "_SE", dig2(Evapotranspiration), "_LV", dig1(licvolfactor), sep = "")) |>
  mutate(names_climate_scenario = paste("SR",dig1(Rainfall), "_SE", dig2(Evapotranspiration), sep = "")) |>
  mutate(names_climate_scenario = factor(names_climate_scenario, levels = unique(names_climate_scenario))) |>
  mutate(names_MDBA_climate_scenario_long = case_when(names_climate_scenario == "SR1.0_SE1.00" ~ "Historical climate",
                                                      names_climate_scenario == "SR0.8_SE1.07" ~ "Dry climate change",
                                                      names_climate_scenario == "SR1.0_SE1.07" ~ "Median climate change",
                                                      names_climate_scenario == "SR1.2_SE1.07" ~ "Wet climate change"))|>
  mutate(names_MDBA_climate_scenario = case_when(names_climate_scenario == "SR1.0_SE1.00" ~ "Historical climate",
                                                      names_climate_scenario == "SR0.8_SE1.07" ~ "Dry climate",
                                                      names_climate_scenario == "SR1.0_SE1.07" ~ "Median climate",
                                                      names_climate_scenario == "SR1.2_SE1.07" ~ "Wet climate"))|>
  mutate(names_CSIRO_climate_scenario = case_when(names_climate_scenario == "SR1.0_SE1.00" ~ "Historical climate",
                                                      names_climate_scenario == "SR0.7_SE1.07" ~ "Hot and Dry",
                                                      names_climate_scenario == "SR1.0_SE1.07" ~ "Just Hot",
                                                      names_climate_scenario == "SR1.3_SE1.07" ~ "Hot and Wet"))|>
  mutate(names_MDBA_climate_scenario_long = factor(names_MDBA_climate_scenario_long, 
                                  levels = c("Historical climate", "Dry climate change", "Median climate change", "Wet climate change")))|>
  mutate(names_MDBA_climate_scenario = factor(names_MDBA_climate_scenario, 
                                  levels = c("Historical climate", "Dry climate", "Median climate", "Wet climate")))
  
  #Scenario names have change - this is a work around. hopefully in future the metadata and EWR outputs match.
  #scenarios$scenario <- stringr::str_match(scenarios$scenario, '(.*)_(.*)')[, -1][,1]

  #Cut off "_0"
 # scenarios$scenario <- stringr::str_match(scenarios$scenario, '(.*)_(.*)')[, -1][,1]


# Add max
MAX_scenario_scenarios <- scenarios[1,]
MAX_scenario_scenarios[1,]<- NA
MAX_scenario_scenarios[1,1] <- "MAX"

scenarios <- bind_rows(scenarios, MAX_scenario_scenarios)
MAX_scenario_scenarios <- NULL

#other data:
objectives <- causal_ewr$ewr2obj |>
  select(-ewr_code_timing)|>
  distinct()

objectives_for_EWRs <- objectives |>
    select(planning_unit_name, gauge, ewr_code, env_obj)


#NSW Border Rivers has env_obj called "NF" WHY IS THAT APPEARING IN THIS DATA??
```

## Simple figure - 0ne climate - without adaptation - model comparison

```{r}
#| label: fig-sdl-comparison

# Scenario comparison for different Sustainable Diversion Limit areas. This example shows the mean proportion of environmental watering requirements (EWRs) that are achieved under each scenario for each SDL unit. This approach illuminates broad-brush differences between scenarios and geographic locations, but does not address which EWRs may be more important to environmental assets or which assets are more sensitive to particular scenarios. Climate scenarios and adaptation options as in @tbl-scenarios. Panels a and b illustrate the same data with a emphasizing quantititive differences and b emphasizing spatial patterns.

#| message: false

sdl_units_aggEWR_NoAdaptation <- sdl_units_aggEWR |> 
  filter(licvolfactor == 1.0) |>
  filter(scenario %in% climate_scenarios) |> 
  arrange(Evapotranspiration, Rainfall) |>
  mutate(scenario = paste(names_climate_scenario, Mk, sep = "_"))

  
sceneorder = factor(sdl_units_aggEWR_NoAdaptation$scenario, levels = sdl_units_aggEWR_NoAdaptation$scenario)

#|>
#  filter(Evapotranspiration == 1.00) |>
#  filter(Rainfall == 1.0) 


Mk_climate_comparison <- ggplot(data = sdl_units_aggEWR_NoAdaptation, aes(x= names_climate_scenario, y = ewr_achieved, fill = Mk)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = pal_Mk) +
  theme_werp_toolkit()

Mk_climate_adapt_comparison <- ggplot(data = filter(sdl_units_aggEWR, !is.na(names_climate_scenario)), aes(x= licvolfactor, y = ewr_achieved, fill = Mk)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~names_climate_scenario, nrow = 3)+
  scale_fill_manual(values  = pal_Mk) +
  theme_werp_toolkit()#+
  #theme(legend.position = 'bottom', axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45))


# The bars
plot_sdl_units_aggEWR_NoAdaptation <- sdl_units_aggEWR_NoAdaptation |> 

  #mutate(scenario = names_climate_scenario)) |> 
  plot_outcomes(outcome_col = 'ewr_achieved',
                outcome_lab = 'Proportion\nEWR achieved',
                x_col = 'scenario',
                x_lab = 'scenario',
                colorset = 'ewr_achieved',
                color_lab = 'Proportion\nEWR achieved',
                pal_list = pal_achieve,
                position = 'dodge',
                setLimits = c(0,1),
                sceneorder = sceneorder) +
  # guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow=2, label.position = 'top')) +
  theme(legend.position = 'bottom')



#MANUAL_sdl_achieve_bars_climate + 

plot_sdl_units_aggEWR_NoAdaptation 

ggsave(plot = plot_sdl_units_aggEWR_NoAdaptation, filename = file.path(comp_results, paste0("sdl_achieve_bars_climate_NoAdaptation", Sys.Date(), ".tiff")), device = "tiff", width = 7, height = 4)

ggsave(plot = Mk_climate_comparison, filename = file.path(comp_results, paste0("barplot_sdl_aggEWR_Mk_climate_comparison", Sys.Date(), ".tiff")), device = "tiff", width = 7, height = 4)

ggsave(plot = Mk_climate_adapt_comparison, filename = file.path(comp_results, paste0("barplot_sdl_aggEWR_Mk_climate_adapt_comparison", Sys.Date(), ".tiff")), device = "tiff", width = 7, height = 5)
```

```{r}
#Edit sdl_target
sdl_target_CSIRO <- sdl_target |>
  filter(names_climate_scenario %in% CSIRO_comparison) |>
  filter(licvolfactor == 1.0)|>
  st_drop_geometry()

#make relative to historic scenario
historic_scenario <- sdl_target |>
  filter(names_climate_scenario == "SR1.0_SE1.00")|>
  filter(licvolfactor == 1.0)|>
  rename(historic_achievement = ewr_achieved)|>
  rename(historic_End_sys = `End sys`)|>
  select(Target, SWSDLName, Mk, env_group, historic_achievement, historic_End_sys)|>
  st_drop_geometry()

sdl_target_edited <- left_join(sdl_target_CSIRO, historic_scenario, by = join_by(Target, SWSDLName, Mk, env_group))|>
  mutate(Achievement = ((ewr_achieved-historic_achievement)/historic_achievement)*100)

#EDit sdl_hydro
sdl_hydro <- sdl_target_edited |>
  distinct(names_climate_scenario, names_CSIRO_climate_scenario, Mk, SWSDLName, `End sys`, historic_End_sys)|>
  mutate(Achievement = ((`End sys`-historic_End_sys)/historic_End_sys)*100,
         Target = "End of system flows") 

sdl_target_edited <- bind_rows(sdl_target_edited, sdl_hydro)


#Edit sdl_economic
sdl_economic$Achievement <- sdl_economic$Economic_outcomes
sdl_economic$Target <- sdl_economic$eco_obj
sdl_economic$Mk <- "Mk4"


#Put together
sdl_env_and_eco <- bind_rows(sdl_target_edited, sdl_economic)|>
  filter(!Target %in% c("Other species", "Priority ecosystem function"))|>
  mutate(Target = as.character(Target))|>
  mutate(Target = factor(Target, levels = c("Native fish","Native vegetation","Waterbird","End of system flows","Water allocation","Agricultural benefits")))|>
  arrange(Target)


#Plot
sdl_env_and_eco |>
  filter(names_climate_scenario %in% CSIRO_comparison) |>
  ggplot(aes(x= names_CSIRO_climate_scenario, y = Achievement, fill = Target, linetype = Mk)) +
    geom_col(position = "dodge") + 
    coord_flip() +
  theme_werp_toolkit()
```

```{r}
#attempting to make lines.
sdl_env_and_eco <- sdl_env_and_eco |>
  dplyr::ungroup()|>

  dplyr::mutate(
    xend = ifelse(Target == dplyr::first(Target),

    yend = ifelse(Target == dplyr::first(Target), 
                  dplyr::last(Achievement), lag(Achievement)))|>
  #will workout how to complete the loop another time - last line going back around the same way as previous line
    # xend = ifelse(Target == dplyr::first(Target), 
    #               dplyr::last(as.character(Target)), lag(as.character(Target))), 
    # yend = ifelse(Target == dplyr::first(Target), 
    #               dplyr::last(Achievement), lag(Achievement)))|>
  dplyr::mutate(xend = factor(xend, levels = unique(Target)))|>
  mutate(Order = as.numeric(Target))


#Attempt to make background
background_df <- data.frame(Order = as.factor(seq(1, length(unique(sdl_env_and_eco$Target)))),
                            Target =  factor(levels(sdl_env_and_eco$Target), levels = levels(sdl_env_and_eco$Target)), y = 320,
                            names_CSIRO_climate_scenario = unique(sdl_env_and_eco$names_CSIRO_climate_scenario)[1])|>
    mutate(Order = as.numeric(Target))


#MAKE PLOT
plt <- ggplot(sdl_env_and_eco,
      aes(
      x = reorder(stringr::str_wrap(Target, 6), Order),
      y = Achievement,
      colour = names_CSIRO_climate_scenario)) +
  
  #Make background colours
    geom_col(data = background_df,
           aes(x = reorder(stringr::str_wrap(Target, 6), Order), y = y, fill = Target), colour = NA, width = 1, alpha = 0.3)+
    geom_col(data = background_df,
           aes(x = reorder(stringr::str_wrap(Target, 6), Order), y = -150, fill = Target), colour = NA, width = 1, alpha = 0.3)+
  
  # Make custom panel grid
  geom_hline(
    aes(yintercept = y),
    data.frame(y = c(-100, 0,100, 200, 300)),
    color = "grey40", linetype = "longdash"
  ) +
  # Add dots to represent the mean gain
   geom_point(size = 3) +
   geom_line() +
  
  # Lollipop shaft for mean gain per region
  geom_segment(
    aes(
      x = stringr::str_wrap(Target, 6), y = -150, 
      xend = stringr::str_wrap(Target, 6), yend = 310),  
    linetype = "solid", color = "gray20",arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"), type = "closed")) + 
  
  #connect points
    geom_segment(
    aes(
      x = stringr::str_wrap(Target, 6), y = Achievement, 
      xend = stringr::str_wrap(xend, 6), yend = yend),  
    linetype = "solid", linewidth = 1) + 
  
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-150, 400))+
  # Make it circular!
  coord_polar()+
  theme_werp_toolkit()+
  theme(text = element_text(size = 20))+
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_CSIRO, aesthetics = "colour") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_Target, aesthetics = "fill")

plt
```

\## fig-causal-example

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| include: false

#| label: fig-causal-example
#| fig-cap: The toolkit incorporates causal networks that describe the environmental objectives for a system. In the current example these causal networks are extracted from the Murray-Darling Basin Long Term Watering Plans (LTWPs), which sets environmental watering requirements (EWRs), objectives, and long-term targets for key water-dependent plants, waterbirds, fish and ecosystem functions. From left to right, the columns here represent EWR codes, proximate Environmental Objectives, Specific Goals, Target Groups, and 5-year Management Targets.

edges <- make_edges(dflist = causal_ewr, 
               fromtos = list(c('ewr_code', 'env_obj'), 
                              c('env_obj', 'Specific_goal'), 
                              c('Specific_goal', 'Target'), 
                              c('env_obj', 'target_5_year_2024')),
               gaugefilter = gauges_to_plot[1]) 

nodes <- make_nodes(edges)


# To work with both html and word, save out and read back in.
causal_example <- make_causal_plot(nodes,
                 edges,
                 focalnodes = filter(nodes, NodeType == "ewr_code")$Name,
                 edge_pal = 'black',
                 node_pal = list(NodeType = 'nationalparkcolors::MtRainier'),
                 render = FALSE,
                 save = TRUE,
                 savedir = 'images',
                 savename = 'causal_structure') 

# if (knitr::is_html_output()) {

patchwork::wrap_plots(causal_structure_grob)
```

```{r}
#EWR scale

  group_by(scenario, ewr_code, SWSDLName, planning_unit_name,
           # env_obj, Specific_goal, Objective, Target, Target_Category,
           # target_5_year_2024, target_10_year_2029, target_20_year_2039,
           Rainfall, Evapotranspiration, licvolfactor, Tributary, `GS Irrig`,

           names_climate_scenario, names_MDBA_climate_scenario_long, names_MDBA_climate_scenario) |>
  summarise(ewr_achieved = mean(ewr_achieved),
            n_versions_of_EWR = sum(n_versions_of_EWR),
            n_gauges = n())

#EWR scale
# Aggregate planning units to SWSDL
ewr_code_SWSDLName <- ewr_code_planning_unit |>
  group_by(scenario, ewr_code, SWSDLName,
           # env_obj, Specific_goal, Objective, Target, Target_Category,
           # target_5_year_2024, target_10_year_2029, target_20_year_2039,
           Rainfall, Evapotranspiration, licvolfactor, Tributary, `GS Irrig`, 
           `HS Irrig`, OFH, Residential, `Link Loss`, `Storage Loss`, `End sys`,
           filename, node_type_10.2, node_type_10.3, node_type_3, node_type_8,
           node_type_8.2, node_type_9, node_type_9.1, names_scenario,
           names_climate_scenario, names_MDBA_climate_scenario_long, names_MDBA_climate_scenario) |>
  summarise(ewr_achieved = mean(ewr_achieved),
            n_versions_of_EWR = sum(n_versions_of_EWR),
            n_gauges = sum(n_gauges),
            n_planning_unit = n())
ewr_code_SWSDLName$names_climate_scenario <- factor(ewr_code_SWSDLName$names_climate_scenario, levels=c(rev(levels(scenarios$names_climate_scenario))))

#Objective scale
#Objectives have to be joined to gauge level data
ewr_code_to_objectives_gauge <- left_join(ewr_code, objectives, by = join_by(ewr_code, gauge))
# ewr_code_to_objectives_gauge <- left_join(ewr_code_to_objectives_gauge, causal_ewr$obj2target)
# ewr_code_to_objectives_gauge <- left_join(ewr_code_to_objectives_gauge, causal_ewr$obj2yrtarget)
ewr_code_to_objectives_gauge <- ewr_code_to_objectives_gauge |>
filter(!is.na(env_obj)) # not all EWRS for each gauge are needed for an objective?

# Aggregate gauges
ewr_code_to_objectives_planning_unit <- ewr_code_to_objectives_gauge |>
  group_by(scenario, ewr_code, SWSDLName, planning_unit_name,
           env_obj, 
           # Specific_goal, Objective, Target, Target_Category,
           # target_5_year_2024, target_10_year_2029, target_20_year_2039,
           Rainfall, Evapotranspiration, licvolfactor, Tributary, `GS Irrig`, 
           `HS Irrig`, OFH, Residential, `Link Loss`, `Storage Loss`, `End sys`,
           filename, node_type_10.2, node_type_10.3, node_type_3, node_type_8,
           node_type_8.2, node_type_9, node_type_9.1, names_scenario,
           names_climate_scenario, names_MDBA_climate_scenario_long, names_MDBA_climate_scenario) |>
  summarise(ewr_achieved = mean(ewr_achieved),
            n_versions_of_EWR = sum(n_versions_of_EWR),
            n_gauges = n())

# Aggregate planning units
ewr_code_to_objectives_SWSDLName <- ewr_code_to_objectives_planning_unit |>
  group_by(scenario, ewr_code, SWSDLName,
           env_obj, 
           # Specific_goal, Objective, Target, Target_Category,
           # target_5_year_2024, target_10_year_2029, target_20_year_2039,
           Rainfall, Evapotranspiration, licvolfactor, Tributary, `GS Irrig`, 
           `HS Irrig`, OFH, Residential, `Link Loss`, `Storage Loss`, `End sys`,
           filename, node_type_10.2, node_type_10.3, node_type_3, node_type_8,
           node_type_8.2, node_type_9, node_type_9.1, names_scenario,
           names_climate_scenario, names_MDBA_climate_scenario_long, names_MDBA_climate_scenario) |>
  summarise(ewr_achieved = mean(ewr_achieved),
            n_versions_of_EWR = sum(n_versions_of_EWR),
            n_gauges = sum(n_gauges),
            n_planning_unit = n())

# Aggregate EWRs
objectives_SWSDLName <- ewr_code_to_objectives_SWSDLName |>
  group_by(scenario, SWSDLName,
           env_obj, 
           # Specific_goal, Objective, Target, Target_Category,
           # target_5_year_2024, target_10_year_2029, target_20_year_2039,
           Rainfall, Evapotranspiration, licvolfactor, Tributary, `GS Irrig`, 
           `HS Irrig`, OFH, Residential, `Link Loss`, `Storage Loss`, `End sys`,
           filename, node_type_10.2, node_type_10.3, node_type_3, node_type_8,
           node_type_8.2, node_type_9, node_type_9.1, names_scenario,
           names_climate_scenario, names_MDBA_climate_scenario_long, names_MDBA_climate_scenario) |>
  summarise(ewr_achieved = mean(ewr_achieved),
            n_versions_of_EWR = sum(n_versions_of_EWR),
            n_gauges = sum(n_gauges),
            n_planning_unit = sum(n_planning_unit),
            n_ewr_code = n())

objectives_SWSDLName$env_group <- stringr::str_extract(objectives_SWSDLName$env_obj, "^.{2}")  
ewr_code_to_objectives_SWSDLName$env_group <- stringr::str_extract(ewr_code_to_objectives_SWSDLName$env_obj, "^.{2}")  

# Aggregate Objectives
groups_SWSDLName <- objectives_SWSDLName |>
    group_by(scenario, SWSDLName,
           env_group, 
           # Specific_goal, Objective, Target, Target_Category,
           # target_5_year_2024, target_10_year_2029, target_20_year_2039,
```

```{r}
objectives <- causal_ewr$ewr2obj |>

  group_by(PlanningUnitID, gauge)|>
  filter(gauge %in% c("421001", "421004", "421012", "421022", "421090"))|>
  distinct(PlanningUnitID, gauge, ewr_code)|>
  mutate(ewr_code = factor(ewr_code, levels = c("CF", "VF", "BF1", "BF2", "SF1", "SF2", "SF3", "LF1", "LF2", 
                                                "OB-WL","OB-WM", "OB-WS1", "OB-WS3", "OB-WS4")))|>
  arrange(ewr_code)|>
  summarise(n_EWR = n(),
            EWRs = paste(ewr_code, collapse = "; ")) |>
 arrange(PlanningUnitID, gauge)
  
ewr_code_to_objectives <- objectives|>
  group_by(ewr_code, env_obj)|>
  filter(gauge %in% c("421001", "421004", "421012", "421022", "421090"))|>
  mutate(ewr_code = factor(ewr_code, levels = c("CF", "VF", "BF1", "BF2", "SF1", "SF2", "SF3", "LF1", "LF2", 
                                                "OB-WL","OB-WM", "OB-WS1", "OB-WS3", "OB-WS4")))|>
  distinct(ewr_code, env_obj)|>
  select(ewr_code, env_obj) |>
  group_by(ewr_code)|>
  summarise(n_env_obj = n(),
            env_obj = paste(env_obj, collapse = "; ")) |>
  arrange(ewr_code)
```

## Hydrographs

```{r}
#| label: fig-ewr-example
#| fig-cap: !expr glue::glue("EWR are illustrated at two example gauges ({paste0(gauges_to_plot, collapse = ' and ')}) on the historical base level (scenario E1) hydrographs. See @sec-ewr-table for a table.")

#Hydrographs- just read in the ones we use
scenehydros <- read_hydro(hydro_dir,
                          # scenariofilter = "historical_Rainfall_1_2_evap_1_0_licvolfactor_1_5_0",
                          long = TRUE, format = 'nc') 

#Scenario names have change - this is a work around. hopefully in future the metadata, hydrographs, and EWR outputs match.
scenehydros$scenario <- stringr::str_match(scenehydros$scenario, '(.*)_(.*)')[, -1][,1]

scenehydros <- left_join(scenehydros, scenarios, by = 'scenario')

# # This relies on the NSW ewr definitions. We could keep passing them around, but better to pull from py-ewr directly
pdi <- reticulate::import("py_ewr.data_inputs")

# The second is 'bad', so just get the first
ewrs_in_pyewr <- pdi$get_EWR_table()[[1]]

NSWEWR_gauge <- filter(ewrs_in_pyewr, Gauge %in% gauges_to_plot) |>
  tidyr::separate_wider_delim(cols = Code, delim = '_',
                              names = c("Code", "Timing"),
                              too_few = 'align_start',
                              too_many = 'merge') |>
  rename(gauge = Gauge) |>
  group_by(gauge) %>%
  distinct(Code, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(FlowThresholdMin = as.numeric(FlowThresholdMin)) |>
  arrange(FlowThresholdMin) %>%
  mutate(Date = seq(from = max(scenehydros$Date),
                    to = min(scenehydros$Date),
                    length.out = n())) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
## | label: fig-obj_in_groups
## | fig-cap: "Proportion of EWRs achieved for each environmental objective, grouped into broader environmental groups (EF = Priority Ecosystem Function, NF = Native Fish, NV = Native Vegetation, OS = Other Species, WB = Waterbirds). This view provides an assessment of the performance of individual environmental objectives, as well as how those contribute to the overall sensitivity of the broader groups across space. Not all EWR are applicable in all locations and there are not equal number of EWR in each category. The MAX column illustrates the total number of EWRs for reference, with each black box showing the situation where all EWRs contributing to an Environmental Objective are met. Where the max column does not exist, those objectives are not relevant to that particular planning unit. This illustration includes three climate scenarios: A (0.5x), E (historical base level/no change), and I (2x) and three adaptation options 1 (no adaptation), 2 (+250 ML/d), and 3 (+6500 ML/d)"
## | message: false
## | warning: false

obj_in_groups <- sdl_objectives |>
  ungroup()|>
  dplyr::filter(scenario != "MAX") |>

  mutate(scenario = paste0(licvolfactor),
        SWSDLName = stringr::str_replace(SWSDLName, '–', '-\n')) |>
  #rename(env_obj2 = env_obj)|>
  plot_outcomes(outcome_col = 'ewr_achieved',
                outcome_lab = "EWR achievement\n (summed proportion of objectives)",
                x_lab = "Climate & adaptation option scenario", 
                colorgroups = 'env_group',
                colorset = 'env_obj',
                pal_list = pal_env,
                color_lab = "Envionmental objectives",
                facet_col = 'names_MDBA_climate_scenario',
                facet_row = 'env_group',
                #sceneorder = sceneorder
                )+ 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust=1))+
  guides(fill=guide_legend(ncol=3))+
  facet_grid(env_group~names_MDBA_climate_scenario, scales = "free")
```

## End of system flows - adaptation comparison

the current scenarios overlap a lot - but this may be a useful plot with other scenarios.

```{r}
#| label: fig-difference-baseline
#| fig-cap: "Quantitative scenario comparison for Native Fish objectives for three SDL units. Scenarios defined here as the difference in mean flow (GL) from the baseline historical scenario (E1). A key message here is that the lines are not smooth- EWR achievement is not simply a function of the amount of water. Instead, the 'adaptation' options, particularly the '2' scenarios of adding 250 ML/d of water, have disproportionately large impact (steep slopes). Shading indicates different environmental objectives within the native fish target group. This illustration includes three climate scenarios: A (0.5x), E (historical base level/no change), and I (2x) and three adaptation options 1 (no adaptation), 2 (+250 ML/d), and 3 (+6500 ML/d)."
#| message: false

scenarios_end_sys <- sdl_objectives |>
  dplyr::filter(names_climate_scenario %in% MDBA_comparison) |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario != "MAX") |>
  mutate(scenario = names_scenario) |> 
  group_by(scenario, env_group) |>
  mutate(y = 0.45,
         'ewr_achieved' = 0.3,
         pointgroup = 1)

gl_difference <- sdl_objectives |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario != "MAX") |>
    dplyr::filter(names_climate_scenario %in% MDBA_comparison) |>
   mutate(scenario = names_scenario) |> 
  plot_outcomes(outcome_col = 'ewr_achieved',
                outcome_lab = "Proportion EWR achieved",
                x_col = "End sys",
                x_lab = "End of system flow (GL)",
               colorgroups = 'env_group',
               colorset = 'env_obj',
               pal_list = pal_env,
                # base_lev = 'E1',
                # comp_fun = 'difference',
               # group_cols = c('env_obj'),
                color_lab = "Envionmental objectives",
                facet_row = 'env_group',
                facet_col = '.'
                ) +
  ylim(0,1) +
  geom_vline(mapping = aes(xintercept = `End sys`),
             colour = "black", linetype = "solid")+
    guides(colour=guide_legend(ncol=3))+
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-contour
#| fig-cap: Condition results visualised as a surface with the two scenario definitions on the axes. This approach allows visualising changes in outcome as the result of multiple axes on which scenarios might differ. These axes might be different aspects of scenario creation (as here), or they might be different axes describing the outcome of scenarios (e.g. two different hydrometrics such as mean flow and flow variance)

# This would be better if we had a more even and tighter set of scenarios
contour_heatmap <- agg_envgroup_sdl_to_plot |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario %in% scenarios_Evapotranspiration_climate_comp) |>
  dplyr::filter(env_group != 'EB') |> 
  mutate(scenario = paste0("SE",Evapotranspiration, "_LV",licvolfactor)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = `End sys`, y = `GS Irrig`, z = ewr_achieved)) + 
  geom_tile() + # OR geom_point
  facet_grid(. ~ env_group) +
  geom_contour_filled(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.1)) + 
  theme_werp_toolkit() 

# This is for Galen's reference for developing the function, I think- overlay points and change the fill ramp

# Changing the fill for geom_contour_filled needs bins. The easiest way to make that work from a continuous scale is to get the colors and then use manual.
binpal <- paletteer::paletteer_c('grDevices::Plasma', n = 10)

contour_point_heatmap <- contour_heatmap +
  # Change the fill scale
  scale_fill_manual(values = binpal) +
  # ideally, we'd use the same color ramp and fill these points with a black circle around them. But that conflicts with the binned fill for the contour
  # geom_point(shape = 21, color = 'black')
  geom_point(mapping = aes(color = ewr_achieved)) +
  paletteer::scale_color_paletteer_c('grDevices::Viridis')

contour_heatmap
contour_point_heatmap
```

2.  Fig of relative vulnerability of types of economic outcomes (Mark IV model?) Impact of degree of climate change and climate variability on those vulnerabilities Do these relative vulnerabilities change with degree of change or degree of variability?
3.  Fig of consistency of environmental outcomes (Mark IV model?)
4.  Fig of consistency of types of economic outcomes (Mark IV model?) Allocation reliability and resilience – supporting economic outcomes, where is the loss in water found across the water balance (Supporting information). Effects of plausible adaptation Can changing the delivery model for environmental water, or the total amount of water recovered to support the environment alter those vulnerabilities?
5.  Relative change in flow duration curves for HEW vs Model Mark IV and V
6.  Resultant impacts on environmental outcomes
7.  Resultant impacts on economic outcomes Tailoring environmental flow delivery can reduce vulnerability Small changes targeting individual environmental water requirements can support environmental function without requiring large new volumes of water
